input.contentScopeRationale: The assignment (LAB-MATH-C, Festival Team Challenge) asks for independent transfer across four surfaces of one idea: equal-groups multiplication in word problems (items 1, 5), equal-row/array structure with commutativity (items 4, 8), missing-factor / division-as-unknown-factor reasoning (items 2, 3), and fact reasoning via nearby known facts plus discriminating a multiplication situation from addition or sharing (items 6, 7). The teacher's target is not the specific numbers but the underlying structure: a multiplication expression names a number of equal groups and a group size, and the same structure can be read from an array, recovered from a missing factor, and derived from a nearby fact. I therefore prescribe a program that teaches equal-groups structure and its array/missing-factor readings with fresh festival-free and festival-adjacent contexts and fresh number pairs, rather than re-asking the eight worksheet questions. Scope is limited to whole-number factors 1-10 with products to 100; no formal division notation, no two-step algebraic notation, no fractions, no multi-digit multiplication. Program size is minimal but sufficient: one shared diagnostic-teaching node before the fork, two route nodes that carry different responsibilities (array/commutativity structure vs. missing-factor/derived-fact reasoning), and one optional bonus node. Quest and Boss remain locked because no real child evidence exists yet.

concept.name: Equal-groups multiplication and its array and missing-factor readings
concept.statement: A multiplication expression a x b names a groups of b equal objects; the same total can be seen as an array of a rows of b, read either way because a x b = b x a, and any one of the three quantities (groups, group size, total) can be recovered when the other two are known.
concept.instanceScope: LAB-MATH-C 'Festival Team Challenge', Grade 3, 2026-08-08. Whole-number factors 1-10, products to 100. Covers equal-groups word problems, two-step-within-one-context group problems, 4-by-9 style array equation writing, unknown-factor problems written as ___ x 8 = 48 or as equal-row sharing, discriminating a multiplication story from an addition or sharing story, and correcting a wrong product by stepping from a nearby known fact. Excludes formal division symbol, remainders, fractions, and multi-digit factors.
prerequisites: Repeated addition of a single addend
Reading and writing an equation with one unknown blank
Recognizing rows and columns in a rectangular arrangement

input.academicTheory: Theory: the child's difficulty on this assignment is not fact recall alone but unstable mapping between a situation and the equal-groups structure that licenses multiplication. When the structure is explicit (7 teams of 6), a child can often skip-count to an answer without ever naming which number is the group count and which is the group size. That fragile mapping predicts three failures visible on this worksheet: treating a two-part group problem as a single multiplication or a bare addition (item 5), writing only one equation from an array because commutativity is not seen as two readings of one picture (item 4), and stalling on unknown-factor items because the missing number is not perceived as a group count to be recovered (items 2, 3). The instructional move is therefore to make the group/group-size/total triple explicit and reversible in one representation (equal groups and arrays), and to teach derived-fact reasoning as a structural step (5 x 9 is one group of 9 more than 4 x 9, or one group of 9 less than 6 x 9) rather than as a recall correction. If the mapping is taught explicitly, later independent and delayed performance on unrehearsed transfer items should improve most on unknown-factor and array-equation items, which are the items least supported by rote skip counting. The fork tests which entry point consolidates the mapping: a spatial-array route or a reversible-equation route, with academic purpose and difficulty held comparable.

assumptions.claim: The child can often reach a product by skip counting but does not reliably name which factor is the number of groups and which is the group size, which is what the assignment's array and unknown-factor items require.
assumptions.uncertainty: There is zero observed performance data for this child; the claim is inferred from the assignment's construction and from the fact bank being empty. The child may already have solid structural mapping and only a fact-fluency gap, which would make the shared node too easy.

assumptions.claim: Unknown-factor items (___ x 8 = 48; 40 flags in 5 equal rows) will be the lowest-accuracy surface at delayed independent testing relative to direct equal-groups items.
assumptions.uncertainty: The concept id math.multiplication.missing_factor is on record but carries no outcome data, so prior exposure could have already resolved this; ordering of difficulty may reverse if the child has memorized the 8s facts.

assumptions.claim: On a two-part equal-groups problem (3 booths x 8 cups, twice), the child is more likely to report a single-step product or a bare sum than the full total.
assumptions.uncertainty: No observed work samples exist. Two-step error rates in grade 3 vary widely with reading load rather than multiplication understanding, so a wrong answer may be a comprehension artifact and not evidence about the concept.

assumptions.claim: The child can produce one equation from an array but not reliably the commuted partner, treating 4 x 9 and 9 x 4 as different facts rather than two readings of one array.
assumptions.uncertainty: Item 4 asks for two equations, which may mean the teacher has already taught commutativity and is checking retention rather than introducing it; if so the assumed gap does not exist.

assumptions.claim: No factual engagement, reward, or route-preference history exists for this child, so route assignment must be treated as an open experiment and no format may be assumed motivating.
assumptions.uncertainty: Absence of records could reflect a logging gap rather than a genuinely new learner; if prior sessions exist elsewhere, the experiment's baseline assumptions would need revision.

assumptions.claim: No catalog candidate has an assignment-specific frozen academic contract or verified artifact hash, so no node in this program may be marked reuse.
assumptions.uncertainty: Runtime status could change before build; if a contract is frozen and hash-verified in time, a revise decision could become a reuse decision without changing the academic content.

assumptions.claim: Because this is the first program for this child on this concept, every baseline node must yield practice_only evidence and cannot support a mastery claim.
assumptions.uncertainty: If the classroom teacher supplies graded independent work for this assignment, that external evidence could support mastery inference sooner than this program can.

learningResponsibilities.title: Name the equal-groups structure in a situation
learningResponsibilities.purpose: Establish whether the child can identify group count, group size, and total in a situation and state which multiplication expression matches, before any route-specific teaching.
learningResponsibilities.academicTarget: Given an equal-groups situation or a competing addition/sharing situation, identify the number of groups and the size of each group and select or write the matching multiplication expression.

learningResponsibilities.title: Read one array two ways
learningResponsibilities.purpose: Test whether spatial array structure consolidates the mapping, including producing commuted equation pairs and generating alternative equal-row decompositions of a fixed total.
learningResponsibilities.academicTarget: From a rectangular array, write both multiplication equations that describe it, and build more than one equal-row array for a given total.

learningResponsibilities.title: Recover a missing factor and derive from a nearby fact
learningResponsibilities.purpose: Test whether reversible-equation reasoning consolidates the mapping on the surfaces least supported by rote skip counting.
learningResponsibilities.academicTarget: Solve for an unknown factor presented as an equation blank or as an equal-sharing-into-rows situation, and correct a wrong product by stepping one group up or down from a known nearby fact.

learningResponsibilities.title: Optional unrehearsed mixed practice
learningResponsibilities.purpose: Offer additional assignment-aligned practice that produces practice_only signal only; it is never required, never gates the board, and cannot support mastery.
learningResponsibilities.academicTarget: Apply equal-groups structure across mixed unrehearsed surfaces (word situation, array reading, unknown factor) with no new concepts introduced.

fork.hypothesis: After a shared structure-naming node, a spatial array-first route and a reversible-equation-first route will produce comparable immediate accuracy, but they will differ in which transfer surface is strongest at delayed independent testing: the array route should advantage commuted-equation and multiple-decomposition items, while the equation route should advantage unknown-factor and derived-fact items. If both routes produce indistinguishable delayed profiles, the entry representation is not the active ingredient and the shared structure-naming node is doing the work.
heldConstant: Six practice items per route node
Mix of response modes: at least one numeric, one construction, and one explanation per route node
Exclusion of formal division notation, remainders, and multi-digit factors
practice_only evidence limit on every node
Starting support level: one worked structural model, then faded to independent attempts
Same delayed-transfer horizon for both preregistered predictions

routes.academicRationale: Enters the equal-groups mapping through the rectangular array, where group count and group size are simultaneously visible as rows and columns, making commutativity and alternative decompositions the primary reasoning objects.

Enters the same mapping through the equation, treating the unknown as whichever slot is blank so that missing-factor and nearby-fact derivation become the primary reasoning objects while the underlying equal-groups structure is identical.

academicHeldConstants: Comparable response-mode mix (numeric, construction, explanation) in both routes
Same starting support: one worked model then faded independence
No new concepts beyond the shared node in either route

routes.engagementHypothesis: With no engagement history on record for this child, a route whose reasoning objects are laid out spatially may sustain longer continuous work because progress is visible without recall; this is a hypothesis only and no prior factual event supports it.
routes.predictedOutcome: If chosen, expect completion of at least 5 of 6 items with no more than 2 assistance requests, and stronger accuracy on commuted-equation and multiple-decomposition items than on the unknown-factor item embedded in the node.
routes.uncertainty: Zero prior sessions means the predicted completion band is essentially uncalibrated. Spatial construction items can also raise interaction difficulty, which would depress completion for input reasons rather than academic ones.
falsifyingEvidence: More than 3 assistance requests across the node
Accuracy on commuted-equation items at or below accuracy on the unknown-factor item
Interaction-difficulty flags on construction items exceeding numeric items
Immediate switch to the other route after the first item

routes.engagementHypothesis: A route framed as recovering a hidden number may sustain engagement through resolution of a stated unknown; with no engagement records for this child, this is an untested hypothesis and not a preference claim.
routes.predictedOutcome: If chosen, expect completion of at least 5 of 6 items with no more than 2 assistance requests, and stronger accuracy on unknown-factor and nearby-fact-derivation items than on the array-reading item embedded in the node.
routes.uncertainty: Unknown-factor items may be the child's weakest surface, so early errors could depress persistence and confound engagement signal with difficulty. No prior latency or frustration data exists to separate the two.
falsifyingEvidence: More than 3 assistance requests across the node
Accuracy on unknown-factor items at or below accuracy on the array-reading item
A run of 3 consecutive incorrect responses followed by disengagement
Immediate switch to the other route after the first item
